hypotheses: Field: both take x (or u) transcendental over a base field, with k general in the lemma and K ⊆ ℂ in the target, so no conflict. The hint is written for one polynomial ring, and I did not settle ℚ versus ℚ̄ in its print. Dimension: they differ. The lemma gives an infinite-dimensional E in k[x], polynomials only, of positive degrees in the hint, so no constants and no negative exponents. The target takes finite S ⊂ ℤ, Laurent, and its consequences need 0, ±1 in S. Conclusion: they differ. The lemma is existence of one space with Property (A B; C 0), for matrices of all ranks. The target is an iff for p×q rank-one configurations, for every S. Conjugation: absent from the source, and the target's core theorem does not use it either. Genericity: same, transcendence only. Key mismatch: every target hull contains {-1,0,1} = {0,1}+{-1,0}, hence a 2×2 configuration, hence fails Property (A B; C 0). So the lemma's spaces are never the target's hulls.
passage: "There exists a k-vector subspace E of k[x] of infinite dimension" (Lemma 12.15*, p. 431)
source_read: Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren 326, Springer 2000. Page images pp. 424, 431, 443, from the library copy of https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/dalag.pdf (same byte size as live file). The given author link is only a 4-page contents. Roy 1989 not read.
explanation: The citation is accurate: Lemma 12.15*, Property (A B; C 0) on p. 424, and Exercise 12.9 with its hint (degrees t_{n+1} ≥ 2t_n), attributed to Roy 1989 Prop. 1. But it does not cover the target. Property (A B; C 0) does exclude 2×2 configurations (my derivation, since a rank-one block forces B or C to vanish). So the lemma says only that some lacunary polynomial span has none. There is no sumset criterion, no iff, no p×q and no Laurent exponents. Nothing addresses k = 2, 3, the pairs of powers, or 2×3 in hulls containing 0, ±1, where 2×2 configurations always exist. Ratio 2 does not transfer either: S ⊇ {-1,0,1,2} carries a 2×3, so 2×3-freeness needs the target's own argument. The nearest contact is the powers u^{4^j} alone (t_n = 4^n), a shared lacunarity idea, assuming the hint is valid. A grep for "sumset" and "geometric progression" in the book's text layer found nothing. The entry may fairly cite this as a nearby degree-lacunarity example, not as prior art. The lemma also covers all matrix ranks, so neither statement implies the other.
